sections.title: Absolute Donor Contraindications
content: 1- Death from unknown cause
2- Systemic infections: HIV, HCV, HBV, Syphilis, Rubella, T.B, Septicaemia, Malaria
3- Prior high-risk behavior for HIV and Hepatitis (Gay, Prostitution, Drug abuse)
4- Last 12 months: Sex with someone who has engaged in high-risk behaviour, received blood clotting factor concentrate, tattooing, ear/body piercing
5- CNS infectious/degenerative diseases: Creutzfeldt Jakob, systemic sclerosing, panencephalitis, Alzheimer, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, MS and Motor Neurone disease
6- Receipt of transplanted organ
7- Receipt of human pituitary derived growth hormone
8- Brain or spinal surgery before 1992
9- Haematological malignancies
10- Ocular factors: Ocular diseases, malignant ocular tumors and corneal refractive surgery

sections.title: Signs of Graft Rejection
content: Ciliary injection & Anterior uveitis
Epithelial rejection: Elevated line of abnormal epithelium (avg. 3 months post-op)
Sub-epithelial rejection: Subepithelial infiltrates (Krachmer spots) resembling adenovirus; deeper edema
Stromal rejection: Deeper haze (chronic/hyperacute)
Endothelial rejection: Linear pattern of KPs (Khodadoust line) at graft margins
Stromal edema: Signifies endothelial failure

sections.title: Management of Graft Rejection
content: Step 1: Preservative-free topical steroids hourly/24h (tapered over weeks)
Step 2: Steroid ointment at bedtime during tapering
Step 3: High-risk maintenance: Prednisone acetate 1% 4x daily for extended periods
Step 4: Cycloplegia 2x daily
Step 5: Topical Ciclosporin 0.05% (note: delayed onset)
Step 6: Oral Prednisolone 1mg/kg daily (1-2 weeks) with subsequent tapering
Step 7: IV Methylprednisolone 500mg daily (up to 3 days) for severe episodes
Step 8: Subconjunctival Dexamethasone (0.5 ml of 4mg/ml)
Step 9: Systemic immunosuppressants (Ciclosporin, Tacrolimus, Azathioprine)

sections.title: Toxoplasmosis Investigations
content: I. Serology: IgM, IgG levels
II. PCR: Testing of intraocular fluid
III. Goldman-Witmer Coefficient: Ratio between IgG in aqueous to IgG in serum
IV. Imaging: OCT, B-scan U/S, Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) to monitor activity
